item.problem: Lesson 6 is described as introducing 'the third major bond type', but Lessons 3 to 5 have already covered ionic, covalent and intermolecular bonding, which makes metallic the fourth. The wording is inconsistent.
item.quote_a: This is the first of the bond-type lessons (ionic, then covalent, then intermolecular forces, then metallic)
item.quote_b: completing the bond types (ionic, covalent, intermolecular forces, metallic) before students investigate the four structure types in Lessons 7-9

items.recommendation: Reword Lesson 6 so metallic is the fourth item in the sequence, matching Lesson 3 and the Lesson 6 wording that follows.
items.reason: Lessons 3-5 already cover ionic, covalent and intermolecular forces, so calling metallic 'third' contradicts Lesson 3's own ordering.

edit.old: introduces the third major bond type — metallic bonding —
edit.new: introduces the fourth bond type in the sequence (after ionic, covalent and intermolecular forces) — metallic bonding —

items.reference: Lesson 3 purposeInStoryline lists the sequence ionic, covalent, intermolecular forces, metallic; the three bond-type rows in the Lesson 6 comparison table (ionic, covalent, metallic) are a separate count and are not affected.
